Modern.brandNameRationale: The cover note — the temporary written confirmation a broker issues a client between application and policy, a piece of insurance vocabulary that has been standard market practice since the 19th-century London market. Strongest of Agent A's three for modern: 'Lloyd & Coffee' risks Lloyd's trademark territory, 'Syndicate 1688' is fine but reads niche. Cover Note is the document every broker sends — instantly readable as insurance, no trademark exposure.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern insurance distribution in 2025+ is being remade by digital brokers and embedded insurance. The category is fragmenting between the legacy commercial broker, the consumer-facing insurtech (Lemonade, Hippo), and the embedded API (Cover Genius). The opening is for a brokerage that talks plain English about the document trail.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Lemonade (lemonade.com) holds the consumer-D2C tier. Newfront (newfront.com) is the modern commercial broker peer. Embroker (embroker.com) sits in the SMB middle. Hippo (hippo.com) does the home tier. We sit closer to Newfront in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A digital brokerage that issues the cover note the day you apply.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Founder or operator at a 10-200 person company. Has been through one broker who took three weeks to bind coverage. Wants a portal, a real human, and a one-page summary.
behaviors: Forwards the policy PDF to the COO without reading it
Will switch brokers over slow renewal
Treats insurance as a procurement line item, not a relationship

dos: Name the document by its industry term
Show the bind date and the rate up front
Send the cover note within the hour

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only — Cover Note in a tight modern grotesk, two words on one line. A small horizontal rule beneath, suggesting the signature line on a broker's note. The rule alone is the favicon.

colorPalette.name: Bind Orange
colorPalette.meaning: Single accent. The colour of the bind-confirmation stamp.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for policy numbers and bind dates
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries document data; the regular carries the brand.

Luxury.tagline: Property and fine-art cover, in the original fire-office tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: The Hand-in-Hand Fire and Life Insurance Society, founded London 1696 after the Great Fire of London (1666); its fire-mark (two clasped hands) was nailed to insured buildings across Georgian London. Strongest of Agent A's three for luxury: 'Equitable Life House' is historically apt but generic-sounding; 'Dodson & Co' is too actuarial for the luxury client. Hand-in-Hand has a visual mark (the clasped hands) baked into its history and reads warm rather than cold — perfect for HNW property and fine-art clients.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury property and fine-art insurance serves the collector, the multi-property owner, and the family office. The category is dominated by Chubb's Masterpiece, AIG Private Client Group, and PURE. The opening is for a brand that revives the Georgian fire-office aesthetic for the same market.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Chubb Masterpiece (chubb.com) holds the institutional peer position. AIG Private Client Group (aig.com) sits at the same tier. PURE (pureinsurance.com) is the modern HNW peer. Hiscox (hiscox.com) does the boutique middle. We sit smaller, more crafted than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A property and fine-art insurer in the Georgian fire-office tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 70. Multi-property HNW owner with a collection — art, wine, watches. Works with a family office and a private banker. Buys the relationship, not the rate.
behaviors: Calls the named broker, never the call centre

dos: Send the fire-mark plaque with the policy

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with a small embossed fire-mark — two clasped hands inside a quartered shield — used on the policy folio, the certificate, and the cast bronze plaque sent with every binder.

colorPalette.name: Fire-Mark Bronze
colorPalette.meaning: The cast plaque on the insured wall.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and policy folio
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure client portal
typography.rationale: A high-contrast classical serif sets the Georgian tone; the grotesk handles the handful of digital surfaces.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: 'Perils' — the specific causes of loss enumerated in every property policy (fire, theft, windstorm, etc.); the building block of all insurance contract language since the 17th-century marine policy form. Strongest of Agent A's three: 'Indemnity' is technically pure but reads cold and legalistic; 'The Underwriter' is good but a job title rather than a concept. Peril is the actual unit policies are written around, single word, archaic-feeling, exactly the kind of trade-word minimalism Agent A's catalog favors.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal insurance brands serve the buyer who wants to read the policy in five minutes and pay in one. The opening is for a specialty broker that publishes covered perils in plain English on a single page.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Lemonade (lemonade.com) holds the consumer-minimal slot. Kin (kin.com) does the no-frills home tier. Sure (sureapp.com) is the embedded peer. We sit closer to commercial specialty than any of them.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A specialty broker named for the unit of risk.

targetAudience.primary: Small-business owners and individual buyers who want one page, one named contact, and the perils listed in English. They don't want a relationship; they want a policy.
behaviors: Will switch brokers over a confusing renewal letter
Pays annually, in full, by ACH

dos: List the perils on the home page
Show the price and the deductible

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. PERIL set in a single-weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps, five letters with generous space. No icon. The page, the policy PDF, and the renewal letter all carry the wordmark and nothing else.

typography.rationale: One face. The page, the policy, and the renewal letter all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.tagline: Commercial-lines underwriting at the historic centre of the trade.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Lombard Street, London — the historic centre of British insurance and banking since the 14th century, named for the Italian (Lombard) merchants who first set up there; Lloyd's moved here in 1691. Strongest of Agent A's three for corporate: 'Tontine Partners' is historically rich but obscure to most procurement buyers; 'Mutual Assurance Co' references Franklin's Philadelphia Contributionship which is more US-regional. Lombard Street is broadly recognised across both UK and US commercial-insurance buyers as the centre of the trade.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate commercial-lines underwriting in 2025+ serves brokers and large risk-managers. The market is consolidating around AIG, Chubb, Travelers, and Zurich, with specialty layers underneath. The opening is for a mid-market underwriting group with discipline on specialty lines (cyber, D&O, marine).
Corporate.competitorLandscape: AIG (aig.com) holds the global commercial peer. Chubb (chubb.com) sits at the same tier. Travelers (travelers.com) is the US commercial leader. Beazley (beazley.com) does the Lloyd's specialty peer. We sit smaller, specialty-focused.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A specialty commercial-lines underwriting group, Lombard Street in posture.

targetAudience.primary: Insurance brokers, large-account risk managers, and CFOs at mid-market commercial buyers. They place specialty lines through a small panel of underwriters and value technical depth over rate.
behaviors: Places risks through a named underwriter

dos: Lead with line-of-business specialty and underwriting appetite
Speak the language of brokers and risk managers

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left — a single Lombard arch reduced to one rounded shape, suggesting the arched colonnade of the historic street. Reads cleanly on a broker submission, a wording, and a renewal letter.

typography.primary: Inter for digital and broker submissions
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed wordings and quarterly commentary
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across underwriting decks; the serif handles printed wordings.

Creative.tagline: Property insurance with a plaque on the wall.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The cast-iron or lead 'fire mark' plaques mounted on insured buildings in 17th-19th century Britain so private fire-brigades knew which houses to save; the original visual brand of insurance. Strongest of Agent A's three for creative: 'The Lutine Bell' is iconic but obscure outside the Lloyd's room; 'Names & Co' could read confusing. Fire Mark Studio gives the brand a real visual artefact — a plaque sent with every policy — that is intrinsically shareable.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative D2C insurance brands in 2025+ are rare; Lemonade did the friendly-illustration version and Hippo did the home-tech version. The opening is for a brand that revives the fire-mark as a literal customer artefact — every policyholder gets a plaque.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Lemonade (lemonade.com) holds the illustrated-D2C slot. Hippo (hippo.com) does the modern home tier. Kin (kin.com) is the no-frills peer. Toggle (gettoggle.com) sits in the renter tier. We sit closer to Lemonade in posture, with a physical artefact.
Creative.positioningStatement: A D2C property insurer that mails you a fire mark with your policy.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 40. Renter or first-time homeowner. Renting from Zillow, owning from Redfin. Wants the policy to feel less like a contract and more like a small piece of design.
behaviors: Hangs the fire mark by the front door
Renews automatically as long as nothing breaks

dos: Mail a cast fire mark with every binding
Write the policy in plain English
Sign the welcome letter by the underwriter

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark and a hallmark. Fire Mark Studio in a chunky display serif, with a quartered-shield fire-mark icon — clasped hands inside a flame outline — that ships as a physical cast plaque to every policyholder.
